reason: The passage demonstrates a critical failure of leadership accountability. King David learns of Amnon's rape of his half-sister Tamar (וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֔ד שָׁמַ֕ע אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַדְּבָרִ֖ים - 'And King David heard all these things') and becomes angry (וַיִּ֥חַר ל֖וֹ מְאֹֽד). However, the narrative provides no indication that David takes any action to hold Amnon accountable, punish him, or restore justice to Tamar, despite her implicit plea for intervention (וְעַתָּה֙ דַּבֶּר־ נָ֣א אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ - 'and now speak to the king'). This failure of the king to enforce justice or accountability for a grave crime committed by his own son illustrates how leadership neglects responsibility for the welfare of their people, even in cases of serious abuse.
